description: A ten-panel composite figure combining SEM micrographs, an EDS spectrum, particle-size histograms and EDS elemental maps, all concerning mechanically milled Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 low-density high-entropy steel powder. (a-d) are SEM micrographs of powder milled 10 h, 20 h, 30 h and 35 h, each with a 2 µm scale bar; (d) is outlined in blue and annotated "Full area". Particle morphology is bulky, irregular and coarse at 10 h and becomes progressively finer and more homogeneous at 35 h. (e) is the full-area EDS spectrum of the 35 h powder: x-axis in keV (0.00-9.00), y-axis counts up to 189, with labelled peaks for C, Mn, Ni and Fe at low energy, Al and Si near 1.5-1.8 keV, a dominant Fe peak near 6.4 keV, Mn near 6.5 keV and further Fe/Ni peaks near 7.0-8.3 keV. (f-i) are histograms of "Particle Size (µm)" versus "No. of Particles" with fitted Gaussian curves and printed average sizes ~10±2, ~6±2, ~5±1.5 and ~4±1 µm. (j) shows a 10 µm-scale-bar SEM image of 35 h powder with analysis spots 1 and 2 plus six EDS maps (Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si, C). Together the panels demonstrate milling-induced particle refinement and a homogeneous elemental distribution in the final powder.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph labelled '10 h MM' with a 2 µm scale bar; coarse, bulky, irregular powder particles of widely varying size with angular, heavily deformed surfaces.
SEM micrograph labelled '20 h MM' with a 2 µm scale bar; particles appear somewhat smaller and more fractured than at 10 h, still irregular.
SEM micrograph labelled '30 h MM' with a 2 µm scale bar; finer, more equiaxed particle population with agglomerated clusters.

SEM micrograph labelled '35 h MM' with a 2 µm scale bar, outlined by a blue frame and annotated 'Full area'; finest and most uniform particle population, marking the field used for the full-area EDS analysis.

Full-area EDS spectrum of the 35 h milled powder; x-axis 0.00-9.00 keV, y-axis counts to 189. Labelled peaks: C (very low energy), Mn, Ni, Fe at the low-energy end; Al and Si near 1.5-1.8 keV; Mn near 5.9 keV; a dominant Fe peak near 6.4 keV with Mn overlap; Fe near 7.0 keV and Ni near 7.5 and 8.3 keV.

Histogram of particle size for 10 h milled powder: x-axis 'Particle Size (µm)' (about 4-22 µm), y-axis 'No. of Particles' (0-60), with a fitted Gaussian curve peaking near 9-10 µm; printed annotation 'Average Size ~ 10 ± 2 µm'.

Histogram of particle size for 20 h milled powder: x-axis about 1-11 µm, y-axis 0-50, fitted curve peaking near 6 µm; printed annotation 'Average Size ~ 6 ± 2 µm'; a bimodal-looking distribution with a secondary bin near 3 µm.
Histogram of particle size for 30 h milled powder: x-axis 0-12 µm, y-axis 0-50, fitted curve peaking near 5-6 µm; printed annotation 'Average Size ~ 5 ± 1.5 µm'.

Histogram of particle size for 35 h milled powder: x-axis about 1-10 µm, y-axis 0-60, fitted curve peaking near 4 µm; printed annotation 'Average Size ~ 4 ± 1 µm'; the leftmost (smallest-size) distribution of the series.

Composite panel: left, SEM micrograph of 35 h milled powder pellet with a 10 µm scale bar and two boxed analysis spots numbered 1 and 2; right, six EDS elemental maps for Fe (dense, magenta), Mn (dense, cyan/blue), Ni (sparse, yellow), Al (sparse, red), Si (sparse, violet) and C (sparse, green), each map carrying its own 10 µm scale bar.

observations.observation: Panels (a)-(d) are SEM micrographs of the milled powder labelled '10 h MM', '20 h MM', '30 h MM' and '35 h MM', each carrying a 2 µm scale bar.
Panel (d) is distinguished by a blue frame and the annotation 'Full area', marking the field used for the full-area EDS measurement.
Visual comparison of (a) to (d) shows the powder population becoming finer and more uniform with longer milling, with the coarsest, most bulky particles in (a).
The EDS spectrum (e) plots intensity on a count axis up to 189 against an energy axis of 0.00-9.00 keV, and its tallest peak is labelled Fe near 6.4 keV.
In spectrum (e) the highest-energy labelled features are Fe near 7.0 keV and two Ni peaks near 7.5 keV and 8.3 keV, while Al and Si appear as two distinct peaks near 1.5-1.8 keV.

The four particle-size histograms (f)-(i) all use 'No. of Particles' as ordinate and 'Particle Size (µm)' as abscissa, with printed average sizes ~10 ± 2 µm, ~6 ± 2 µm, ~5 ± 1.5 µm and ~4 ± 1 µm respectively.
The fitted distribution maxima shift monotonically to smaller particle size across (f) to (i), from near 9-10 µm in (f) to near 4 µm in (i).
In panel (j) the Fe and Mn elemental maps are the most densely populated, whereas the Ni, Al, Si and C maps show only sparse, isolated signal.
Panel (j) contains two numbered analysis spots, 1 and 2, marked on the 35 h milled powder SEM image for point EDS analysis.

The caption states that (a-d) show the morphology of powder samples milled for different times, that (d) is the 35 h powder used for full-area EDS, and that (e) is the EDS spectrum of the 35 h powder showing the elements of the final composition.

The caption assigns panels (f-i) to the particle-size distributions of the 10 h, 20 h, 30 h and 35 h milled samples respectively and states that the average powder particle size decreases as milling time is prolonged.
The caption states that the SEM micrograph in (j) shows light and dark grey contrasts corresponding to a BCC phase rich in Fe and a γ-brass type structure rich in Mn, respectively.
The citing text reports three contrasts (white, light grey, dark grey) in the 35 h micrograph and states the mean particle size of the 35 h powder is 3-5 µm.
The citing text states the particle sizes were measured using ImageJ software and that Table 3 lists the elemental composition of the 35 h milled powder from the full area, spot 1 and spot 2.
The citing text assigns the light grey contrast to BCC (ferritic, Fe-rich) and the dark grey contrast to γ-brass type (Mn-rich) structure, confirmed by chemical analysis of the 35 h milled powder.

unreadable_items: panel (e): individual keV tick labels and the exact count-axis maximum are small at the supplied resolution, so peak energies are read to about ±0.2 keV rather than exactly
panels (f)-(i): individual histogram bin counts and bin edges are not labelled, so only the fitted distribution shape and the printed average sizes can be quoted
